title: Calculus 1
semester: 15-week semester · 12 instructional units · Week 15 review and assessment
description: A full first-semester differential calculus pathway from limits through derivatives, applications, curve analysis, optimization, and a preview of integration.
outcomes: Evaluate limits algebraically and use continuity, including the Intermediate Value Theorem, to reason about function behavior.
Compute derivatives from the definition and apply power, product, quotient, chain, trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, implicit, and inverse differentiation rules.
Interpret derivatives as slopes and instantaneous rates in tangent-line, motion, related-rates, and approximation problems.
Use derivatives and the Mean Value Theorem to locate extrema, analyze graph shape, and solve clearly stated optimization problems.
Find basic antiderivatives and evaluate simple definite integrals using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

units.title: Limits and Limit Laws
units.summary: Develop the limit as the value a function approaches, distinguishing nearby behavior from the function's value at the point. Use limit laws for direct substitution and algebraic methods such as factoring and expanding to remove zero-over-zero forms, while checking that any cancellation is valid only near the limiting point.
objectives: Evaluate polynomial and rational limits using direct substitution and limit laws.
Use factoring or expansion to evaluate selected indeterminate zero-over-zero forms.
Combine known function limits with constant multiples, sums, and differences.

units.title: Continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem
units.summary: Connect continuity at a point with the agreement of the limit and the function value, and use one-sided information to choose parameters in piecewise functions. Apply the Intermediate Value Theorem only on a closed interval where continuity is known, using endpoint signs to guarantee an intermediate output without confusing that guarantee with a formula for locating it.
objectives: Determine parameter values that make piecewise functions continuous at a joining point.
Verify the continuity and endpoint hypotheses needed for the Intermediate Value Theorem.
Use intermediate-value conclusions to identify or compute guaranteed function values.

units.title: Derivative Definition and Tangent Rates
units.summary: Define the derivative as the limit of a difference quotient and interpret it simultaneously as tangent slope and instantaneous rate of change. Contrast average rates over intervals with instantaneous rates at a point; when evaluating the definition, simplify the quotient before letting the increment approach zero to avoid treating an indeterminate form as an ordinary value.
objectives: Evaluate derivative limits from simplified difference quotients at specified points.
Use differentiation to determine the slope of a tangent line at a given point.
Interpret a position function's derivative as instantaneous velocity in a motion model.

units.title: Power Rule and Polynomial Derivatives
units.summary: Move from the limit definition to efficient shortcuts for constants, powers, constant multiples, sums, and differences. Extend the power rule to fractional and negative exponents after rewriting radicals and reciprocals, taking care with exponent subtraction, constant terms, and restrictions inherited from the original function's domain.
objectives: Differentiate polynomial functions term by term using the power and constant-multiple rules.
Rewrite radical and reciprocal terms as powers before differentiating them.
Track signs and constant terms accurately when differentiating combinations of powers.

units.title: Product and Quotient Rules
units.summary: Differentiate products and quotients without incorrectly distributing differentiation across multiplication or division. Organize the product rule as first times second's derivative plus second times first's derivative, and keep the quotient numerator's subtraction order explicit before simplifying or factoring the result.
objectives: Apply the product rule to products of polynomial factors and simplify the derivative.
Apply the quotient rule with the correct numerator order and squared denominator.
Choose algebraic simplification that preserves every factor and sign in a derivative.

units.title: The Chain Rule
units.summary: Recognize compositions by identifying an outer function and an inner function, then multiply the outer derivative evaluated at the inner expression by the inner derivative. Practice nested powers, roots, and reciprocals while watching for missing inner factors, unintended expansion, and parentheses that change which expression is raised to a power.
objectives: Identify outer and inner components in algebraic compositions before differentiating.
Differentiate composite powers, roots, and reciprocals with the complete inner derivative.
Apply the chain rule more than once when differentiating nested compositions.

units.title: Trigonometric, Exponential, and Logarithmic Derivatives
units.summary: Build the standard derivatives of sine, cosine, tangent, natural exponentials, and natural logarithms, with angles measured in radians. Combine these rules with the chain and product rules, paying special attention to negative inner coefficients, the natural-log convention, and equivalent forms such as sec²x = 1/cos²x for the derivative of tangent.
objectives: Differentiate combinations of sine, cosine, and tangent using radian-based rules.
Differentiate natural exponential and logarithmic functions with composite arguments.
Combine elementary derivative rules with product and chain rules in mixed expressions.

units.title: Implicit and Inverse Derivatives
units.summary: Differentiate both sides of a relation with respect to x, treating y as an implicit function so every y term acquires the appropriate dy/dx factor. For inverse functions, use the reciprocal derivative relation at corresponding input-output points, verifying the point correspondence and a nonzero original derivative rather than merely reciprocating at the same coordinate.
objectives: Compute tangent slopes on implicitly defined curves by differentiating both sides.
Collect and solve for dy/dx while retaining product-rule and chain-rule terms.
Evaluate inverse-function derivatives at corresponding points using the reciprocal relation.

units.title: Related Rates
units.summary: Translate changing geometric quantities into an equation relating their values, then differentiate that relationship with respect to time before substituting the instantaneous data. Keep known constant dimensions separate from changing measurements, include every chain-rule time derivative, and use signs to distinguish increasing quantities from decreasing ones.
objectives: Differentiate geometric relationships with respect to time to connect instantaneous rates.
Substitute measurements only after differentiating and solve for the requested rate.
Interpret positive and negative rates consistently in area, volume, and motion contexts.

units.title: Linearization, Differentials, and Newton's Method
units.summary: Use the tangent line at a nearby known point to approximate function values, and interpret the differential dy = f'(x)dx as the corresponding linear change rather than the exact increment. Apply Newton's update formula with the current function and derivative values, keeping the subtraction sign and substituting the current iterate throughout the formula.
objectives: Construct and evaluate local linearizations to approximate nearby function values.
Compute differentials from a function value, derivative, and specified input change.
Perform one Newton's-method iteration for a nonlinear equation using an initial estimate.

units.title: Extrema, the Mean Value Theorem, and Curve Analysis
units.summary: Locate critical numbers and combine them with endpoints to determine absolute extrema on closed intervals. Use the Mean Value Theorem to connect average and instantaneous rates after checking its hypotheses, then use first derivatives for monotonicity and second derivatives for concavity and inflection points without assuming every critical point or zero second derivative produces the corresponding feature.
objectives: Find critical numbers and evaluate candidates to determine extrema on closed intervals.
Verify Mean Value Theorem conditions and solve for an interior point with the required slope.
Use second-derivative sign changes to identify inflection coordinates and describe curve shape.

units.title: Optimization, Antiderivatives, and Definite-Integral Preview
units.summary: Model optimization problems with an objective function and a constraint, reduce to one variable over a physically meaningful domain, and justify the optimum using derivatives and endpoints. Reverse differentiation to find antiderivatives with an arbitrary constant, then connect definite integrals with net accumulation and area by evaluating an antiderivative at the two bounds; Week 15 remains available for synthesis and assessment.
objectives: Optimize constrained geometric models and justify the requested maximum or minimum value.
Find polynomial, exponential, and trigonometric antiderivatives including the constant of integration.
Evaluate simple definite integrals by subtracting endpoint values of an antiderivative.
